brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.evidence: 3 joined bases (piece:0,0,0, 1,0,0, 0,1,0) with 3 joint bolts make one free-standing block. check_build passed with meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: The catalog has no iron holder. accessory:0#0,0#3 is a rod socket, made to stand a round tube up off a cell face, so it can carry a bought iron sleeve or stand. Whether a printed part is safe next to a hot iron depends on the material, and the configurator cannot check that. Heat resistance is unmet: use a metal stand or sleeve and keep the hot tip away from printed parts.
bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-half, shown with a solder reel in it.
bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-half-div2, a half-depth bin with 2 compartments to keep tips sorted.

finish.summary: Three full bases sit in a triangle, joined by three joint bolts. Cell 1,0 has a half-depth bin for solder, with a solder-reel prop in it. Cell 0,1 has a half-depth bin with 2 compartments for spare tips. Cell 0,0 is kept for the iron: the catalog has no soldering-iron holder, so I put a rod socket (hex-acc-rod) on its outer side. That socket can carry a bought metal iron sleeve. Rule check passed and the mesh-collision check reads clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Blank plug
parts.use: Fills an insert recess you are not using, so the face reads flat and the pocket stays clean.

parts.name: Female socket
parts.use: Seats in a recess and takes a stud, which makes it the bottom of every stacked insert.

parts.name: Male stud
parts.use: Threads through a seated socket and stands proud of the face, so it can carry whatever mounts above it.

parts.name: Foot
parts.use: Snaps onto a stud to give the face something to stand on, so a cell can rest on its cover rather than on its rim.

parts.name: Zip-tie anchor
parts.use: Seats in a recess and gives a cable tie something to pass through, so a bundle is anchored to the face instead of looped around it.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.

parts.name: Port plug
parts.use: Blanks a side port you are not using, so a cell that is closed up looks finished and nothing gets in through a hole you left open.

parts.name: Port louvre
parts.use: Vents a closed cell without letting rain in, so a box that has to breathe can still stand outside.

parts.name: Port screen
parts.use: Passes air and keeps insects and debris out, so a cell can breathe through an opening that is still covered.

parts.name: Port hose barb
parts.use: Lands a hose on a cell, so water arrives and leaves through a spigot drawn for it rather than over an edge.

parts.name: Port cable plate
parts.use: Leads cable through a side port on finished holes, so wiring enters a closed cell through something drawn for it and each run has its own way in.
